title: 1998 AMC 8 Problem 20
statement: Let \(PQRS\) be a square piece of paper. \(P\) is folded onto \(R\) and then \(Q\) is folded onto \(S.\) The area of the resulting figure is \(9\) square inches. Find the perimeter of square \(PQRS.\)

solutions.text:
After the two folds, the resulting triangle has area \(9.\) Four congruent copies of this triangle make the original square.

So the square has area \(4\cdot 9=36,\) giving side length \(6.\) Its perimeter is \(4\cdot 6=24.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D .
hints: After the two folds, four congruent pieces make the original square.
Use the resulting area to find the original side length.
